helpful: Provisioned petition and BIO text with documents.json metadata: the BIO's alternative-holding vehicle argument drove most of the downward adjustment.
Segment base rate by salience band (sal-v4) with bracketed reached figures and per-row n, which made pooling the prior-Term anchor straightforward.
gaps: fedcourts query has no subject or keyword filter, so priors on a specific doctrine (Quiet Title Act, law of the case, return-trip petitions) cannot be surfaced; the returned priors were unrelated recent grants.
The reply brief was on the docket but not provisioned; a reply-brief document kind would help on cells where the BIO raises a vehicle problem the reply may answer.
No published conditioned cut for the forward relist hazard from a given distribution count, or for the cert-order share of grants, so those claims rest on terminal-bucket arithmetic plus judgment.
A return-trip indicator (prior SCOTUS docket for the same case) in the snapshot or context would be a useful signal; here it had to be read from the petition.
notes: The cvsg-increment claim is structurally impossible on any petition where the United States is already the respondent; a harness-side vacuous mask keyed on a federal respondent would keep those cells from banking near-zero probabilities as if they were forecasts.
